key_insight: This large East Asian GWAS found two new Parkinson’s disease susceptibility loci, plus an East Asian-specific regulatory variant near LRRK2 linked to gene expression and disease risk.
clinical_relevance: The study shows that Parkinson’s genetic risk is partly ancestry-specific, supporting broader representation in genetic research to improve risk discovery across populations.
method: GWAS in 5,825 East Asian participants (3,043 PD cases, 2,782 controls)
Meta-analysis with two additional East Asian cohorts, totaling 74,716 participants
Integrated brain eQTL data to test functional regulatory variation at candidate loci
evidence_signal: The strongest signals were TLE4 (rs10780320; Pmeta_combined = 2.853e-10) and HLA-V/HLA-G (rs11751333; Pmeta_combined = 1.031e-9), and the LRRK2 variant rs1388594 replicated across three East Asian cohorts and reached genome-wide significance in East Asian meta-analysis.
watch_item: These findings are population-specific and the LRRK2 variant was not associated with Parkinson’s disease in European-ancestry datasets, so cross-ancestry generalization is limited.
paper_title: Analysis of east Asian Parkinson's disease Genomes Identifies Novel Susceptibility Loci and Functional Regulatory Variation
